notebooks.title: Provisional Foundations of WAKE Durable Record
notebooks.summary: WAKE models operational state through a deterministic replay of accepted events, ensuring that current state is never cached but derived from an authoritative, append-only SQLite log. Governance acts as the sole validator for proposals, preventing invalid states from entering the durable chain.
notebooks.findings:
State reconstruction in WAKE is strictly deterministic, relying on replay of accepted operations rather than a mutable state cache. [source-c07acfeebe1548f6]

The governance module enforces state validity by rejecting invalid proposals before they are appended to the durable record. [source-be48d836aaf44716]
notebooks.limitations: Current model scope restricted to structural record analysis; lacks runtime verification of concurrent event ingestion.
notebooks.next_questions: Does the atomicity of the SQLite transaction prevent partial writes when a proposal is rejected during the governance check?
notebooks.reason: Revising to integrate governance and record store roles in operational state modeling.

notebooks.title: Foundations of Autonomous Problem Formulation
notebooks.summary: This revision integrates automated value system learning from observations and human demonstrations, showing how preference grounding functions can be inferred in sequential decision-making domains.
notebooks.findings: Value systems can be automatically learned from observations and human demonstrations using preference-based reinforcement learning. [source-52834634309e4d70]
notebooks.limitations: Evaluation is currently restricted to simulated use cases and formal models.
notebooks.next_questions: How do learned value systems scale to open-ended environments without human demonstrations?
notebooks.reason: Revising the foundational inquiry notebook with new preference learning evidence.

notebooks.title: Provisional Foundations of Autonomous Objectives
notebooks.summary: Explores how intelligent systems might derive internal objectives through preference elicitation and multi-objective decision frameworks.
notebooks.findings: Multi-objective Markov decision processes provide a formal foundation for modeling value system acquisition. [source-52834634309e4d70]
notebooks.limitations: Provisional analysis based on current collected literature.
notebooks.next_questions: What mechanisms drive spontaneous objective divergence in unconstrained agents?
notebooks.reason: Establishing provisional synthesis for the unassigned objectives project.

notebooks.title: Instrumental Convergence and Instrumental Succession
notebooks.summary: This notebook explores the limits of standard instrumental convergence theses and how the gradual transfer of agency impacts the rational requirement for continuity preservation in advanced intelligent systems.
notebooks.findings: Standard instrumental convergence and orthogonality theses may require qualification when applied to modern architectures like large language models. [source-859bdb9e925e4f90]
notebooks.limitations: The collected sources highlight a hypothesis-level perspective that requires more formal decision-theoretic backing.
notebooks.next_questions: How do contemporary language model architectures alter the classical derivations of self-preservation drives?

notebooks.title: Provisional Foundations of Mechanistic Complexity
notebooks.summary: This provisional notebook explores the definition of 'mechanism' in the philosophy of science as a prerequisite for investigating unprompted complexity growth in adaptive systems. The current analysis relies on the general framework of mechanistic explanation.
notebooks.findings: Mechanistic explanation in science involves explaining the behavior of a system through the organization and activities of its components. [source-17f73eafdc974002]
notebooks.limitations: This notebook relies on a single source defining the general philosophy of scientific mechanisms and does not yet contain specific evidence on unprompted complexity growth.
notebooks.next_questions: What specific experimental evidence exists for spontaneous complexity increases in non-programmed adaptive systems?
notebooks.reason: Synthesis of the current available evidence as required by the synthesis-ready status of the project.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
